findings.title: The headline promises trust and nothing on the page backs it

location.description: the headline and the "Lock gate times" note

findings.viewer_experience: A harbor master reading "can stand behind" next to "Gate openings are worked out from each tide" cannot tell who does the working out. They must guess whether it is more work for the office or a black box they cannot vouch for.

current.value: The note says "Gate openings are worked out from each tide" with no subject, and the page says nothing about where the tide data comes from, what the office checks, or what Tidewell replaces.

findings.target: The verb has its subject, and the page says where the tide data comes from, what the office checks or approves, and what the office does now.
findings.fix_direction: Give the verb its subject ("Tidewell works out gate openings from each tide...", if that is true). The maker must supply where the tide data comes from, what the office checks or approves, and what the office does now. Do not make these up.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees, in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, that the "Lock gate times" note names who works out the gate openings, and that the page says where the tide data comes from and what the office checks or does now.

findings.title: The feature notes are too narrow on tablet

location.description: the lower row of three feature notes at 768 px

findings.viewer_experience: Each note is 181 px wide, about 20 characters per line, and runs four lines. "Depth at the pontoon" wraps to two lines, which pushes its note 24 px below the other two, so the row looks like a staircase. The reader gets broken, jumpy lines where the product is explained.
findings.target: at least 30 characters per line, with the three notes starting on one line
findings.fix_direction: Below a width where each note gets at least 30 characters per line, stack the notes in one column the way the phone layout does, or set them two and one.
findings.source: Bringhurst on measure; Hochuli on staircases

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of section.points > div.point > p in the tablet viewport is 30 or more, and the three note headings start at the same y or sit one per row

findings.title: The table does not say it is a sample of what berth holders see
findings.viewer_experience: A visitor can read the table as today's real tides, or as a widget, rather than as the page their berth holders would see. The page's best evidence explains less than it could.

current.value: No line under the "Today at Porthmellin" heading says what the table is.

findings.target: One short line under the heading says this is a sample of what berth holders see.
findings.fix_direction: Add one short line under the heading that says this is a sample of what berth holders see.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees, in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, a short line under "Today at Porthmellin" that says the table is a sample of what berth holders see.

findings.title: The table panel's left edge does not line up with any feature column

location.description: the table panel in the hero, left edge at x 664, against feature columns at x 491 and 837

findings.viewer_experience: The hero and the lower row sit on two different grids.

current.value: panel left edge at x 664; feature columns at x 491 and 837

findings.target: The panel starts on the left edge of the second or third feature column, or the columns of the two rows share a width.
findings.fix_direction: Start the panel on the edge of the second or third feature column, or make the columns of the two rows share a width.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees, in the desktop and widescreen viewports, the left edge of the table panel lined up with the left edge of a feature column.
